name: Evening hot shower / bath

card.summary: A warm shower or bath before bed for faster sleep onset; thinly sourced here.
card.note: Very hot water can cause drowsiness or dizziness.

quick.overview:
The practice is a warm shower or bath in the evening to ease into sleep.

Sources reviewed for this wiki do not test the claim.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say the body cools after the bath, signaling sleep.
quick.risks: Very hot water can cause drowsiness; the hot tub article treats that as a drowning risk.[1]

lead: The evening hot shower or bath is a pre-bed routine of washing in warm or hot water shortly before sleep. Proponents say it promotes sleep onset by relaxing the body and, as the body cools afterward, lowering core temperature.[1] For looks, the appeal is the chain from better sleep to a more rested appearance: Wikipedia's sleep deprivation article lists periorbital puffiness, the so-called eye bags, among the effects of too little sleep.[2]

The routine is circulated in sleep and looksmaxxing communities as a simple wind-down habit. Sleep-hygiene guidance in general recommends relaxing activities before bedtime, a regular schedule and a cool, dark, quiet sleeping space, though the Wikipedia article on sleep hygiene does not specifically mention warm baths.[3]

Source material for this entry is thin: the Wikipedia pages on hot tubs and sleep hygiene do not cover the bath-before-bed claim, and the hot tub article notes that sitting in water above normal body temperature can cause drowsiness, which it presents as a drowning risk.[1] Training-forum posters also mention hot baths and showers after exercise in their logs.

chain: Warm shower or bath before bed
Relaxation and later cooling of the body
Easier sleep onset, so a more rested look (less eye puffiness)
angle.text: People use a warm evening wash as a wind-down habit to fall asleep more easily. Better sleep is the link to looks, since lack of sleep is associated with puffy under-eyes and a tired appearance.

infobox: Hot water can cause drowsiness or dizziness

paras: Practitioners take a warm or hot shower or bath in the evening before bed. Proponents attribute faster sleep onset to relaxation and to the temperature change afterward, as the body loses the heat it gained.[1]

Wikipedia's sleep deprivation article lists periorbital puffiness, commonly called bags under the eyes, among the effects of sleep loss.[2] Practitioners who adopt the evening bath as a sleep aid generally frame it as one part of a wider routine of regular sleep timing and a calm, cool bedroom of the kind sleep-hygiene guidance describes.[3]

The hot tub article notes that sitting in water above normal body temperatures can cause drowsiness, which is a drowning risk in that setting.[1] The site note for this entry also lists dizziness as a possible effect of very hot water.
No studies found in the sources reviewed for this entry on evening showers or baths and sleep onset.

lore.intro: A warm evening shower or bath is discussed as a simple sleep aid and wind-down habit.[1][3]

claims.claim: A hot shower or bath before bed helps you fall asleep faster
claims.believers: Proponents report feeling drowsy after bathing and falling asleep sooner.
claims.experts: Sources reviewed here do not examine this claim.
